name: Mendicant-Order Saints
note: Hub for the saints of the Franciscan, Dominican and related mendicant orders of the 13th-15th c.

name: Medieval Women Visionaries
note: Hub for the visionary women mystics of the high and late medieval Latin West.

name: Anselm of Canterbury
cat: Medieval saint / Doctor of the Church
note: Benedictine archbishop and scholastic theologian (1033-1109); venerated saint and Doctor of the Church, father of scholasticism.

name: Peter Damian
note: Camaldolese monk, cardinal and reformer (c.1007-1072); venerated saint and Doctor of the Church.

name: Albertus Magnus
cat: Mendicant founder / Doctor of the Church
note: Dominican friar, bishop and polymath (c.1200-1280); teacher of Aquinas, venerated saint and Doctor of the Church.

name: Thomas Aquinas
cat: Mendicant founder / Doctor of the Church
note: Dominican friar and theologian (1225-1274); the Angelic Doctor, venerated saint and Doctor of the Church.

name: Bonaventure
cat: Mendicant founder / Doctor of the Church
note: Franciscan minister general and theologian (1221-1274); the Seraphic Doctor, biographer of St Francis, venerated saint.

name: Vincent Ferrer
note: Dominican itinerant preacher (1350-1419); apocalyptic missionary, patron of builders, venerated saint.

name: Bernardino of Siena
note: Franciscan Observant preacher (1380-1444); promoter of devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus, venerated saint.

name: Simon Stock
note: Carmelite friar (d. c.1265) traditionally credited with the vision of the Brown Scapular from the Virgin; venerated saint.

name: Julian of Norwich
note: English anchoress and mystic (c.1342-c.1416); author of the Revelations of Divine Love, the first known book in English by a woman; widely venerated.

name: Mechthild of Magdeburg
note: Beguine and Cistercian mystic (c.1207-c.1282); author of The Flowing Light of the Godhead; venerated visionary.

name: Angela of Foligno
note: Franciscan tertiary and mystic (1248-1309); the 'Mistress of Theologians', author of the Memoriale; canonized 2013.

name: Catherine of Sweden
note: Brigittine abbess (c.1331-1381); daughter of Bridget of Sweden, second abbess of Vadstena, venerated saint.

name: Frances of Rome
note: Roman noblewoman, foundress of the Oblates of Mary (1384-1440); mystic granted a visible guardian angel, venerated saint.

name: Vitus
note: Early martyr (d. c.303) whose cult flourished in the medieval West; one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, invoked against epilepsy and 'St Vitus's Dance'.

name: Erasmus of Formia
note: Martyr-bishop (d. c.303), known as St Elmo; one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, patron of sailors.

name: Pantaleon
note: Physician-martyr (d. c.305); one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers in the Latin West, patron of physicians.

name: Eustace
note: Legendary martyr converted by a vision of a stag bearing the Cross; one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, patron of hunters.

name: Cyriacus
note: Roman deacon-martyr (d. c.303); one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, invoked against demonic temptation.

name: Acacius
note: Legendary soldier-martyr (Achatius); one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, invoked against headache and in death-agony.
